subject: baby porcupine
provider: Built-in image_gen; model identifier not exposed by the tool
prompt:
Create one complete full-bleed square image of a single irresistibly cute BABY PORCUPINE character, upright, very simple and memorable. The baby is a chubby soft little ball, like a dumpling wearing a cozy sweater, with a huge head, compact body and tiny tucked feet. It should look gentle, curious and a little clumsy, with absolutely no aggression. Its MOST IMPORTANT identifying feature is a very large rounded rosy pink snout projecting toward the viewer, like a soft gummy candy: a broad rounded squishy oval with two small dark nostrils clearly facing forward. Give the nose only a tiny restrained moist gleam. The face itself is small so that this oversized pink nose feels wonderfully prominent. Two tiny dark round eyes sit on either side of the nose, conveying earnest curiosity and quiet concentration. Use a near-frontal three-quarter view so both eyes and both nostrils are visible. Avoid a smile or an open mouth; the nose and eyes carry the personality.
The body has a cap of SOFT SHORT BABY QUILLS. Portray them graphically as a small handful of broad, rounded, overlapping tufts along the back and crown, a soft scalloped outline with blunt ends, not needle-like spikes and not individual hair strokes. Keep a strong continuous circular outer silhouette. The tiny ears must be low and rounded, never rabbit-like. No visible tail. Keep the whole character reduced to a few broad color masses. Use warm cream for the small face and soft tummy, rich cocoa-plum for the quill cap and tiny eyes/nostrils, and muted rose-pink for the oversized snout. Put it against one perfectly uniform muted lilac background, harmonious with the warm cream and plum. Prioritize the big gummy pink nose over any other detail. Keep the quills, eyes and nose clearly readable when the image is small.
Composition: large visually dominant character emerging from the lower-right, nearly filling the square, with a calm lilac breathing area toward the upper-left. Show enough round body and tiny feet to feel like one soft ball, without adding detailed anatomy. Preserve the full nose and eyes with ample room around them. Keep the main figure upright and the canvas square. Style: ultra-clean graphic character, broad rounded weighty shapes and baby-like proportions. Add an extremely, extremely subtle, almost imperceptible sense of depth through a barely-there neo-skeuomorphic treatment. Do not make it a realistic animal photograph or a heavily rendered 3D toy.
Constraints: single character only, no words, letters, text, watermark, frame, border, scenery, props or added symbols. No thin lines, long needles, sharp tips, fur texture, scattered decorative marks, glossy plastic rendering, dramatic lighting, strong bevels, extrusion or external cast shadow. Only the tiny nose gleam is permitted. Background remains a single uniform lilac color, with normal square outer corners. Approximately 1536 by 1536.
